newsitem.title: BURMA: Thailand, Burma to discuss refugee crisis.
newsitem.headline: Thailand, Burma to discuss refugee crisis.

text.p: Senior Thai and Burmese army officials will meet on Tuesday to try to resolve a refugee crisis after tens of thousands of people fled border clashes between Burmese troops and Karen guerrillas.
Thai Army Commander in Chief General Chetta Thanajaro said in Bangkok on Monday he would meet Burmese Deputy Commander in Chief of Defence Services General Maung Aye.

"We will discuss the overall situation, including refugees," Chetta said in Bangkok on Monday. "If Burma is willing to take them back we will extend our full cooperation...and help them screen out guerrillas from the civilians in the camps."
The meeting will be held at Thachilek in northeastern Burma.
Burmese troops have pressed ahead with a dry season offensive over the past few weeks, sacking several camps of the Karen National Union (KNU) operating in eastern Burma.
The attacks prompted more than 20,000 Karens to flee to Thailand which is already home to almost 100,000 Karen refugees.
The KNU was formed in 1948 to fight for greater autonomy for the Karen state. It is the last major rebel group to have rejected Rangoon's peace overtures and refuse to lay down arms.
Burma said in a statement received on Monday that there had been 53 clashes over the past few weeks, killing 41 KNU members and seven Burmese soldiers.
A spokesman for the KNU, Ner Dah, told Reuters about 100 Burmese soldiers had been killed or wounded but that the fighting had eased over the past few days.
"The situation has improved a lot now," he told Reuters by telephone from the border. "There has been no movement of the Burmese troops in the past two days."
He also dismissed Burmese government statements that 511 KNU members had surrendered to the Rangoon side since February 11.
"That was not a true report," he said.
The announcement came amid talks of a split in the 15,000-strong KNU.
Military analysts said they expected Burma to ask Thailand to be more aggressive in its efforts to halt the border skirmishes.
"They want a change in Thai policy," one said. "They want to put some pressure on the camps."
Last week, senior Thai military officers said they planned to bring order to Karen refugee camps.

"We plan to establish orderly camps for them and strictly screen (KNU) guerrillas out from civilians," Lieutenant General Thanom Vacharapuk said. "Anyone found with arms will be pushed back to Burma."
Thai officials are expected to centralise the sprawling refugee camps which currently house about 60,000 Karens. Another 30,000 refugees are scattered in nearby villages.
